title: Free Will & Determinism
rootClaim: Human beings possess genuine free will, exerting conscious agency and moral responsibility over their choices.

branches.text: First-person subjective experience provides direct, intuitive evidence of conscious deliberation and choice.

children.text: Agent-Causation: Conscious minds act as uncaused initiators of events, distinct from deterministic event-event physical chains.
Moral & Legal Systems: Society logically requires personal agency, praise, and blame for intentional actions.
Retributive Justice: Legal institutions and contractual accountability presuppose genuine moral responsibility rather than puppet causation.

branches.text: Neuroscience indicates that decisions are formulated by pre-conscious neural processes prior to subjective awareness.

children.text: Libet Experiments: Motor readiness potentials in the brain build up hundreds of milliseconds before an agent reports conscious intent.
Epiphenomenal Consciousness: Conscious awareness is a passive observer of neural activity rather than the executive controller.
Veto Power ('Free Won't'): Conscious awareness retains executive power to consciously veto pre-conscious impulses before physical execution.

branches.text: Compatibilism: Free will is compatible with physical determinism when defined as acting on internal desires without external coercion.

children.text: Second-Order Volition: Freedom consists of reflective alignment between higher-order desires and immediate motivations.

branches.text: Hard Determinism: Every physical event, including human brain states, is completely determined by preceding physical causes and natural laws.

children.text: The Luck Problem: If actions are uncaused or quantum-random, they represent stochastic chance rather than intentional free choice.

definitions.description: The capacity of a rational being to make moral judgments and be held morally accountable for actions.
The philosophical view that causal determinism and free will are logically compatible perspectives.
The view that causal determinism is true and completely rules out free will and moral responsibility.
The capacity of conscious awareness to inhibit or veto motor actions initiated by pre-conscious brain processes.
